From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Resourcing bridge request — SRE backfill during review window

Hi team,

Quick context: SRE-2 (internal headcount) will be out for a four-week parental leave starting 6/21 and their resignation notice overlaps with our mid-June performance review period (we need to keep on-call coverage and a minimal handover). Normally we'd open a standard backfill requisition, but with the current company freeze and the timing of performance calibration (6/18–6/25) I'm asking for a short-lived "bridge" exception: a contractor (3–5 weeks) to maintain incident coverage and avoid piling work on the rest of the on-call rotation.

Ask: Can we approve a freeze-exception for a contractor (up to $18k) for a 4-week window, with the caveat that we will not convert to full-time without a subsequent headcount approval? I attached a short headcount impact matrix and the perf-review timeline.

Why this matters quickly: if we don't secure temporary coverage now, we'll push additional on-call burden onto three engineers already flagged in the performance conversations — this creates a morale and calibration risk.

What I propose: 
- A single vendor contractor (SRE generalist) for 4 weeks (6/21–7/18).
- Cost cap $18k (includes vendor fee).
- Approval conditional on (a) no FT conversion without formal HC approval, (b) budget charge to SRE runbooks cost center (run-ops), and (c) weekly check-ins with Laura.

Please reply with approval or tradeoff suggestions. If you want me to route to People Ops or Procurement formally, I can submit the HRREQ ticket now.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, SRE
Redwood Inference
Attachments: headcount_impact_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), perf-review-timeline.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Monica — thanks for the clear ask and for flagging the perf-review overlap. A couple of clarifying points before I sign off:

1) Cost source: can this come from the run-ops discretionary pot, or will we need to reallocate from open hiring budgets (which are tight)?
2) Scope: will the contractor carry primary on-call rotations or just triage/incidents escalation support?
3) Alternatives: are there volunteers for temporary OOO swaps? I want to make sure we consider internal coverage first.

If the contractor is strictly for triage/safety and cost stays under $18k, I'm inclined to approve temporarily, but I need confirmation on (1) and (2). Marcus, can you provide a vendor estimate and confirm whether we can timebox the role to not exceed the cap?

Laura

Thanks for the thread and the clear plan. People Ops is comfortable approving a timeboxed freeze exception for a contractor under the following conditions: 

1) Submit the HRREQ ticket (HRREQ-421) with the attached headcount impact matrix and vendor estimate (Marcus) before EOD 6/11.
2) Contractor term limited to 4 weeks (no conversion without formal HC approval).
3) Charge to run-ops cost center; finance will verify available funds and set the accounting tags.
4) Weekly check-in with Laura on workload impact; if we see sustained burden, we will prioritize FT req in the next hiring cycle.

I'll mark this as approved in the HRREQ queue once the ticket and vendor estimate are attached. Janet — when you have the candidate shortlist please share resumes and the SOW; Monica will handle the technical interview.
